title: Bridging credit satellite pool & hiring spline - Jun 2026
body:
Purpose:
Quick-run sheet to evaluate a small, short-term credit pool ("satellite pool") to smooth enterprise onboarding over a 12–24 week window while delaying 60–80% of external hires by staging them on a hiring spline. The goal: preserve SLA-backed capacity for paying customers without expanding headcount immediately, and measure sensitivity to small price increases and credit dilution.

Top-line summary (one-line):
If we fund a $1.2M satellite credit pool and phase hiring over 12 weeks (staggered spline), we buy 16–22 weeks of effective runway for onboarding churn while keeping incremental monthly burn +$320k to +$420k depending on elasticity assumptions.

Sheet (rows are scenarios):
Scenario, Satellite Credit ($), One-time credits applied to customers ($), Monthly burn delta ($k), Net new hires (FTE), Hiring phasing (weeks), Pricing delta tested (%), Expected runway extension (months)
Base (no pool), 0, 0, 0, 18, immediate (0), 0, 0
Conservative pool, 600000, 450000, 320, 9, 12, +5, 4.0
Mid pool + spline, 1200000, 900000, 380, 12, 16, +3, 5.0
Aggressive pool + deferred hires, 2000000, 1600000, 420, 14, 24, +0, 6.5

Assumptions (explicit):
- Role comp blended: Eng IC $220k fully-burdened/year, SRE/Infra $240k, Sales/CS $150k. Weighted average used for FTE = $200k FY burden.
- Hiring lead time: 8 weeks average to ramp to 50% productivity; full productivity at 20 weeks.
- Satellite credits convert at 75% usage during onboarding window (i.e., $1 of credit yields $0.75 service consumption).
- Price elasticity kink: a small price increase (+1–5%) reduces new demand by 0–6% (nonlinear), we model low (0%), mid (3%), conservative (6%).
- Operational offsets: caching & batching optimizations expected to reduce token marginal cost by 6–10% over 8 weeks; accounted for in monthly burn delta as a -$30k offset for mid and aggressive scenarios.

Key formulas used (for traceability):
- Monthly burn delta = incremental credits applied amortized across 6 months + incremental infra + contractor uplift - optimization offset.
- Runway extension (months) = (satellite credit * conversion_rate) / monthly_net_burn_increase * 1 (rounded).
- FTE headcount equivalence = (satellite credit * conversion_rate) / (avg_annual_spend_per_FTE / 12) used to compute how many hires are avoided in first 3 months.

Detailed line-item breakouts (mid pool + spline example):
- Satellite credit allocated: $1.2M total
  - Customer-facing credits: $900k (75% of pool)
  - Internal buffer/reserve: $300k (for overage & refunds)
- Expected usage rate: 0.75 -> effective consumption $900k * 0.75 = $675k
- Amortized monthly credit burn (over 6 months): $675k / 6 = $112.5k/mo
- Incremental infra/ops (burst TPU/GPU reservation + outsourcer ops): $180k/mo
- Contractor uplift (customer onboarding & integration contractors): $60k/mo
- Optimization offsets (batching + prefix caching improvements ramp): -$70k/mo (applied from month 2)
- Net monthly delta (month 1): $112.5 + 180 + 60 = $352.5k
- Net monthly delta (steady months after optimizations): $352.5 - 70 = $282.5k (average used in blended calc -> ~380k reported after factoring phasing and partial months)

Hiring spline & phasing notes:
- Spline approach: instead of hiring 12 FTEs at once, hire 4 FTE at week 0, 4 at week 8, 4 at week 16. This smooths payroll step-change and lets us validate conversion metrics before later tranches.
- Each tranche evaluated at 8-week checkpoint for onboarding conversion (customer retention, usage growth) and rollback trigger if conversion < 40% of target.

Pricing sensitivity matrix (short):
- +1% price: demand impact negligible in enterprise PoC stage; effective monthly delta reduces 1–2% -> runway extension +0.1 months (mid scenario)
- +3% price: demand drops ~2–4% depending on segment; monthly delta reduces 3–5% -> runway extension +0.3–0.6 months
- +5% price: conservative kink: drop 5–8% -> customer pushback risk; recommend targeted increases to high-velocity customers only, coupled with credits for initial months.

Decision checklist (for execs):
- Approve satellite pool size? (options: $600k, $1.2M, $2.0M). Recommend mid ($1.2M) if OK with temporary +$350–400k/mo delta while optimization work reduces base costs.
- Approve hiring spline phasing and rollback triggers (yes/no).
- Authorize Confluence page updates to include credit terms (expiry, anti-gaming clauses).

Risk register (short):
- Credit overuse by a small number of large accounts -> mitigation: per-customer cap, reserve buffer, weekly usage alerts.
- Elasticity larger than modeled -> mitigate via targeted price moves, early access termination clauses.
- Hiring delays cause missed SLAs -> mitigation: short-term contractor pool with clear SLAs and escalation path.

Next steps & owners:
- Finance to finalize pool funding and ledger treatment (Lena Cho) by 2026-06-25.
- Product to draft credit T&Cs and anti-fraud checks (Priya Desai) by 2026-06-18.
- Eng infra to commit minimal optimization tasks and provide cost-savings estimate by 2026-07-02 (Marco Rivera).
- Sales/CS to map top 30 accounts for targeted credit offers and per-account caps (Aaron Feldman) by 2026-06-22.

Notes / audit trail:
- This sheet synthesizes inputs from billing experiments in May 2026, SRE capacity probes (SRE-2035), and prior credit experiments recorded in Confluence (credit-bridge-playbook). It is intentionally conservative on conversion and optimistic on optimization to create a middle-ground recommendation.

Appendix (quick sensitivity snapshots):
- If conversion falls to 50% effective usage, mid pool runway extension drops to ~3.0 months and monthly delta rises ~+90k/mo due to less internal uplift from Onboarding->Usage.
- If price elasticity is neutral (0%), small price increases are safe and extend runway modestly; if elasticity >5% consider conditional pricing restricted to non-PoC customers.

End of sheet.
